feature: Certified degree-one surrogates reduce expensive curve-image compositions

benchmark.profile: debug, debug symbols level1, incremental disabled
benchmark.baseline_instrumentation: Elapsed-stage logging around existing affine/projected certificates; no fitting-math changes

observations: A source of degree 2..16 can propose a degree-one surrogate using the existing degree-change solver. A complete normalized-parameter bound must certify it within one millionth of the requested error. The source controls, tangent frames and sampling clock remain authoritative in fitting.

The entire surrogate reserve is subtracted with downward rounding. A complete affine or strictly increasing projected correspondence must then certify the surrogate and candidate. Composing the two ordered, onto maps proves the original source within the unchanged total tolerance.

Source degree and control caps bound the optional dense reduction. All construction/proof failures retain the original pipeline. The surrogate performs no closest queries; the existing 255-query and 256-interval budget is unchanged. Each continuous stage retains its exact-work, arithmetic and depth limits.

Regression witnesses cover an actual floating subtraction that rounds upward, a candidate that would exceed the total tolerance if stage limits were added independently, a feature hidden by endpoint degree reduction, common signed weight gauges, parameter domains, model scales, reversal and source nonmutation. Existing retraced-source traversal rejection still passes.

In six saved debug-profile fits, quintic sources previously spent 25–26 seconds in a degree 5 to degree 3 projected image proof. Certified degree-one sources avoid that high-degree composition. The benchmark records single-run timings, not general speed or release/Rhino parity.

Both backends preserve all 217 matching surface records among 231 saved cases and the 14 explicit independent-shape/join-mode counterexamples. All 24 original unequal-source, 24 independent spacing holdouts and 64 representation records remain matched. General adaptive command admission remains unfinished.
